meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В мире всё всегда меняется.
examples.trans: Everything in the world always changes.

examples.text: Строятся и растут новые города.
examples.trans: New cities are built and grow.

examples.text: Рождаются миллионы новых людей.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я сказал, что ты здесь.
examples.trans: I said that you are here.

examples.text: Что тебе надо? Ничего, работаем.

examples.text: Потому что я жду ребёнка, папа.
examples.trans: Because I am expecting a baby, Dad.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Frenchman' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'does', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Do everything that I said right now!

examples.text: Да это она его случайно видела!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Почему он решил готовить до ужина?

meanings.en: to make it, to be in time
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'managed', paired with 'успевать'.

examples.text: Мы должны всегда идти только вперёд.
examples.trans: We must always move only forward.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тебя в зале спрашивает гость.
examples.trans: A guest is asking for you in the dining room.

examples.text: Французский гость, наверное, уже выдал меня.
examples.trans: The French guest probably already gave me away.

examples.text: Катя, что сейчас говорит этот гость?
examples.trans: Katya, what is this guest saying right now?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are afraid of'.

related.gloss: not to are afraid of (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Я не боюсь.
examples.trans: I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Строятся и растут новые города.
examples.trans: New cities are built and grow.

examples.text: Рождаются миллионы новых людей.
examples.trans: Millions of new people are born.

examples.text: Зачем людям летом новые блюда?
examples.trans: Why do people need new dishes in summer?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему ты кричишь на весь ресторан?
examples.trans: Why are you shouting across the whole restaurant?

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

examples.text: Как вы все знаете...
examples.trans: As you all know...

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to replace', paired with 'заменять'.

examples.text: Вы все решили меня здесь заменить?
examples.trans: Did you all decide to replace me here?

examples.text: Никто меня здесь не заменит!
examples.trans: Nobody will replace me here!

examples.text: Заменить арест на подписку.
examples.trans: To replace arrest with a travel ban.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто меня здесь не заменит!
examples.trans: Nobody will replace me here!

examples.text: Витя, никто не хотел тебя менять!
examples.trans: Vitya, nobody was going to replace you!

examples.text: Это просто настоящий праздник для меня, друг!
examples.trans: This is simply a real holiday for me, friend!
